blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence: Two columns, `birthday` (month and day, no year) and `phone`, are added to `profiles`, filled only for members who opt in.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: Store the opt-in explicitly (a consent flag with its date) and define what withdrawing it does: clear `birthday` and `phone` from `profiles` when the member turns the option off, and make the daily job select only opted-in profiles. Add a spec scenario "A member opts out" (WHEN a member turns the option off THEN birthday and phone are erased and no greeting is sent) and a matching task. Today the plan adds only the two columns (tasks.md 1.1), the job selects "the profiles whose birthday is today" with no consent check, and nothing describes opting out: a member who withdraws keeps their birthday and phone in `profiles` and may keep receiving SMS sent through Textly (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), 5(1)(e), Art. 7(3)).
findings.title: Opting out neither erases the birthday and phone nor stops the greetings

findings.evidence:
kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
database into the nightly backups.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: State the retention period of the nightly backups and how an erasure (opt-out or account deletion) reaches them — backup rotation within a stated delay, or re-applying erasures on restore. As written, a member's birthday and phone removed from `profiles` survive in every backup for an undefined time, and a restore brings them back (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17).
findings.title: Birthday and phone kept indefinitely in nightly backups, with no expiry or erasure

findings.evidence:
phone number and display name to Textly's API (hosted in the United
States), which sends the message.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: record Textly as a processor (Art. 28 agreement, record of processing under Art. 30) and name the transfer mechanism for the US (EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification or standard contractual clauses, GDPR Chapter V), or choose an EEA-hosted SMS provider. Also say whether Textly retains the phone numbers and message contents, and for how long. Only the controller can confirm what was agreed.
findings.title: Phone numbers and names transferred to a US processor without a stated safeguard

findings.evidence: Members enjoy being remembered; marketing wants birthday messages.
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: state the purpose (a greeting, or marketing) and the lawful basis — presumably consent through the opt-in (GDPR Art. 6(1)(a); ePrivacy Directive for marketing SMS) — and restrict the phone number to that purpose, so marketing does not reuse it for other campaigns (Art. 5(1)(b)).
findings.title: Purpose and lawful basis of the birthday SMS not stated

findings.evidence: - [Textly is down] → the job retries the next day.
findings.recommendation: Say that the job's failure handling logs only the profile's `user_id` and the error, never the phone number, display name or the request body sent to Textly.
findings.title: What the job logs when Textly fails is not defined
